title: Income tax reassessment - the time limits after recent legal changes
p1:
A tax notice received years after filing a return can feel unexpected.

But did you know that income tax authorities cannot reopen every old assessment whenever they want?
p2: Many taxpayers still believe reassessment can happen indefinitely. The reality is that recent changes have introduced clearer time limits and conditions for reopening cases.
p3:
In simple terms, reassessment allows the tax department to review a past return when there is a reason to believe income may have escaped assessment. Under the newer framework, the usual time limit is generally shorter, while extended periods apply only in specific situations involving higher-value escaped income and required conditions.

The key takeaway: keeping records, responding to notices on time, and knowing the applicable reassessment period can protect taxpayers from unnecessary confusion.
conclusion: Have you ever received a tax notice related to an old assessment? Do you think taxpayers are sufficiently aware of reassessment time limits?
